# Trait polarity

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.9\linewidth]{images/apomorphies.png}
\end{figure}  

- Basal traits: evolved earlier; shared by all
- Derived traits: evolved later; define subclades

\hfill \tiny ([Berkeley: Understanding Evolution](https://evolution.berkeley.edu/evolution-101/the-history-of-life-looking-at-the-patterns//))

# Derived traits in reptiles / birds: occipital condyle

- 1 "ball & socket" vs 2 in mammals

e) b and c  

# Birds are "reptile-hipped" theropod dinosaurs

- Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous **periods** belong to the Mesozoic **era**
- Modern birds survived K-Pg boundary, continuted evolving in Tertiary and Quaternary **periods** in current Cenozoic **era**

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.8\linewidth]{images/dinos.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_classification))

# Evolution both makes new lineages and occurs within them 

- **Cladogenesis**: lineage splitting through speciation; gives rise to new clades
- **Anagenesis**: evolutionary change within a lineage without speciation

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.8\linewidth]{images/dinos.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_classification))


# *Archaeopteryx lithiographica*: A transitional form

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.35\linewidth]{images/berlin.jpg}
\end{figure}  

- Lived ca. 150 mya (late Jurassic); discovered 1861 in Germany and ended up at London NHM
- Like modern birds, had hallux + asymmetrical flight feathers on wings + feathers on tail
- Unlike modern birds, had teeth and long bony tail

\hfill \tiny ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaeopteryx))

# Jehol biota in china fills in Mesozoic gaps

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.8\linewidth]{images/jehol.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny ([*Gansus zheni* by Stephanie Abramowicz in "Birds of Stone"](https://archive.org/details/birds-of-stone-chinese-avian-fossils-from-the-age-of-dinosaurs-pdfdrive))
\normalsize  

- Transitional fossils from ca. 135 - 121 mya (early Cretaceous); discovered 1861 in Germany and ended up at London NHM  
- Diverse taxa and traits including structural color

# Cursorial versus arboreal hypotheses for flight

- **Cursorial**: a running start (chukars do this)
- **Arboreal**: climbing, then gliding, then flapping
- Likely a mix!

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.7\linewidth]{images/flight.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (Rashid et al. 2014)

# Which of the following places derived bird traits in the order they evolved?

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.5\linewidth]{images/jehol.png}
\end{figure}  

a) hollow bones, feathers, four digits in hand, toothless beak
b) toothless beak, four digits in hand, feathers, toothless beak
c) feathers, toothless beak, hollow bones, four digits in hand
e) four digits in hand, hollow bones, feathers, toothless beak
